invariants.value: Every path here is a path route_request answers, and every path route_request answers is here — apart from the empty-string spelling of the root, which no HTTP request line can carry. Every path this table does NOT name answers NOT_FOUND: the fallback is what happens off the table, so it is not an entry on it. answered_by names registered declarations of this package and nothing else.

schema.value: tuple[dict[str, str], ...] constant, ordered as route_request decides. Each entry carries seven keys — path: the path as served, leading slash kept; method: the HTTP method, always GET; purpose: one sentence naming what the caller gets; effects: none (embedded bytes, nothing read) or read (the session's current reading); answered_by: the declarations that produce the answer as canonical module::name ids, comma separated; media_type: the Content-Type of a successful answer; errors: the structured error codes this path can answer with, comma separated, empty where it has none.

intent.value: Every path studi0 serves, declared as data: what a caller asks for, what comes back, which declarations produce it, and what answering costs. The routing decision is still taken in route_request one path at a time — this is that same table said out loud, so a person, a test and a documentation build can all read what studi0 serves without reading a function body and guessing. The two are held in step by tests/test_api.py: a path named here that route_request does not answer, or a path route_request answers that is not named here, fails there.

There is no graph to serve and an empty one would be a lie a viewer could not detect — an empty graph and an unbuilt project look identical on screen — so studi0 names the situation and names the remedy instead.

intent.value: Encodes one JSON-compatible document the way every studi0 response body is encoded — sorted keys, UTF-8 bytes — so identical documents are identical bytes on every machine (INV-5).

Builds one answer carrying an embedded text asset — the page, its stylesheet, its script — encoded as UTF-8 exactly as the build recorded it. studi0 substitutes nothing into an asset on the way out, so what a browser receives is byte-for-byte what the model carries.

Builds one JSON answer — status, content type, encoded body — so every JSON route in the table, answers and errors alike, is labelled and encoded identically and no route can quietly grow its own conventions.

The studi0 local host: a loopback-only HTTP server that serves one page per s0ma project — the sh0w view of the project's own component graph — plus the read-only graph API the page polls. It binds 127.0.0.1 only, answers GET only, and writes nothing at all: the one file studi0 ever puts in the project it is showing is the presence marker its launcher writes (studi0_narration.write_presence), and no request path touches disk.
